intro: The line across a nightclub poster has a different audience from the line across a domestic painting or exhibition interior. Compare where the figure disappears into pattern.
alt: Three views of Microsoft in a limited-color nightclub poster, a pattern-filled room and a gold geometric portrait.

variants.name: Toulouse-Lautrec poster
variants.look: A dark figure and a strong diagonal angle stand out in very few ink colors.
variants.history: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec made color lithographic posters for venues and performers in 1890s Paris.
variants.when: Study how a strong silhouette distinguishes a figure in a setting with many competing details.
variants.why: A figure recognizable by shape can catch the eye of a viewer walking past the poster.

variants.name: Les Nabis
variants.look: The dress and wallpaper meet as neighboring patterns so the figure can briefly blend into the room.
variants.history: Late nineteenth-century artists known as the Nabis explored decorative painting and other media, making designs for interiors, screens and prints as well as easel paintings.
variants.when: Study how pattern can change the way we locate a person inside a room.
variants.why: Related colors and motifs make the surface read across both the furniture and the figure.

variants.name: Vienna Secession
variants.look: A dark silhouette sits against gold and repeated geometric elements.
variants.history: The Vienna Secession was founded in 1897 by artists seeking independent exhibitions. Graphic arts, architecture and decorative design all figured in the movement.
variants.when: Study how one decorative rhythm can carry across several media or across an exhibition room.
variants.why: A consistent set of proportions and repeated forms make individually designed things feel like parts of a shared setting.

prompt: Educational art style comparison board. Exactly 3 equally wide scenes side by side in stated order in a wide 3:1 montage, separations only at vertical boundaries. Recurring original character is an adult woman with ash-blonde hair in a neat low bun, four-color square hair clip, black rectangular glasses worn throughout, black blazer over knee-length black sheath dress, blue lanyard, blank badge, white coffee mug with four colored squares. As specified, she is the subject of each individual artwork's idiom, or a visitor for works that do not depict people. Style distinctions are immediately clear. Scene list in exact order: Toulouse-Lautrec poster idiom black and ochre limited lithographic ink palette, flat woman silhouette and diagonal framing at a late-night venue, no lettering; Les Nabis decorative interior interlocking dress and wallpaper patterns, flat intimate scene in softened cranberry and olive; Vienna Secession brocade-gold and geometric decorated rectangle with flat stark silhouette and a gridded ornamental wall, no wording. No lettering, captions, watermark or ornamental frame.
